kill.text: Price below $70: re-test whether AI agents are eroding the workflow franchise
Subscription revenue growth below 15% for two quarters (Q3 2026: 21%)
Renewal rate below 97% or visible seat losses at large customers
Another large acquisition that adds more than 5% to the share count

sections.industry_map: ServiceNow sells a workflow platform for IT service management, IT operations, HR, customer service and security operations, increasingly with AI agents (Now Assist). It competes with Salesforce, Microsoft, Atlassian, Workday and AI-native start-ups.
sections.size_growth: Enterprise workflow and ITSM software ~$100B+ market growing ~10-12%; ServiceNow subscription revenue $3.99B in Q3 2026 (+21%) (aiweekly coverage of Q3, 29 Oct 2026). Low cyclicality but sensitive to IT budget reallocation toward AI infrastructure.
sections.structure: ServiceNow dominates large-enterprise ITSM (~40%+ share) with high switching costs; the debate is whether AI agents commoditise seat-based workflow software.
sections.demand_supply: Demand for AI agents rising: AI ACV target raised to $1.7B (+70% year to date), agentic consumption up 13x. But Q4 cRPO guide of 18.5% signals deceleration, and management flagged accounting adjustments and deployment-support costs on large deals.
sections.industry_risks: (1) AI disruption of seat-based SaaS - medium/high; warning: net new ACV and seat counts. (2) IT budgets shifting to AI capex - medium/medium; warning: cRPO growth. (3) Post-midterm federal spending changes (US federal is a large vertical) - low-medium/medium.
sections.outlook: Near: subscription growth slowing toward ~18-19%; stock down ~35%+ this year. Mid: if agents are priced on consumption, growth can re-accelerate. Long: the system-of-action for enterprise AI or a slowly shrinking seat franchise.
sections.winners: Owning the workflow data and permissions layer, consumption pricing for agents, trust with CIOs, high retention.
sections.business: Subscription is ~97% of revenue; renewal rate historically ~98%. Free cash flow margin ~30%+, but stock-based compensation is heavy. A 5-for-1 stock split took effect in late 2025 (prices here are post-split).
sections.right_to_win: ServiceNow already sits on top of enterprises' IT and HR processes, so AI agents that act on those processes need its platform and data.
sections.moat: Wide historically (switching costs). Trend: under question as AI agents could bypass seats; keep at narrow-to-wide until growth stabilises.
sections.tam_competitors: Leader in ITSM; competitors Salesforce Agentforce, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Atlassian, Zendesk, plus AI start-ups. Runway: CRM and security workflows, AI consumption revenue.
sections.management: CEO Bill McDermott (since 2019, ex-SAP) is a strong seller; capital allocation has turned acquisitive (goodwill now 76% of equity per ValueInvestor research) and the company announced another layoff round after the slide. Insider selling small ($3.7M over 6 months).
sections.financials: Revenue $4.5B (2020) to $13.3B (2025), GAAP operating margin 4% to 14%, FCF $1.4B to $4.6B. ROIC ~15%. Net debt 2.0x EBITDA flagged (acquisition debt). Diluted share increase in the data is distorted by the 5:1 split.
sections.company_risks: (1) Growth deceleration - KPI: cRPO growth (guide 18.5%). (2) Pricing model transition - KPI: AI ACV vs seat ACV. (3) Acquisition integration - KPI: goodwill impairments. (4) SBC dilution - KPI: share count.
sections.variant_view: The market now prices ServiceNow as a SaaS name disrupted by AI; we think its workflow data layer makes it a beneficiary of agents, but proof is needed, so the stock is fairly valued rather than a bargain.
sections.valuation: Our value (owner earnings after stock compensation $3.4/share, 16% then 10%, 9.5% discount): low $65, base $117, high $170; price $102 implies ~14% growth. Street mean $156 (46 analysts). Peers: ~26x forward EPS vs CRM ~20x, ADBE ~16x. Required margin of safety 35% (quality under question) gives entry $76; Ming's cost $87 (+17%).
sections.pillars: (1) Subscription growth above 17% - breach below 15%. (2) AI ACV keeps compounding - breach: target cut. (3) FCF margin above 30% - breach below 25%. (4) Renewal rate ~98% - breach below 97%.
sections.catalysts_flow: Q4 2026 results (late Jan 2027) with 2027 guide; Knowledge 2027 (May). Sellers: growth funds rotating out of application software. Buyers: GARP funds if AI ACV accelerates.
sections.premortem: (1) AI agents from Microsoft/Salesforce replace ServiceNow seats. (2) Growth slips to low teens and the multiple compresses further. (3) A large acquisition destroys value.
